title: 2.2.12 Flowchart a Decision
description: Draw the ticket-price algorithm as a flowchart. One start, one decision diamond with two labelled exits, one end.

aiGrader.prompt:
Draw a flowchart for this algorithm:

1. Start.
2. Get the customer's age.
3. If the age is under 13, the ticket costs $8. Otherwise the ticket costs $14.
4. Print the ticket price.
5. End.

Use an oval for Start and for End, a rectangle for each task, and a diamond for the decision. Label both arrows leaving the diamond so a reader knows which answer goes which way.

rubric.title: Gets the age before deciding
rubric.description: A task or input shape that obtains the customer's age appears on the path between Start and the decision diamond. Credit any reasonable wording — 'get age', 'ask for age', 'input age'. Deny if the diagram jumps straight from Start to the decision with no step that obtains the age.

rubric.title: Diamond asks the right question
rubric.description: The decision diamond tests the customer's age against 13 — for example 'age < 13', 'under 13?', 'age less than 13'. Accept an equivalent inverted test such as 'age >= 13' as long as the branches below it are consistent with the direction of the test. Deny if the condition tests a different number or a different quantity.

rubric.title: Both prices appear on the correct branches
rubric.description: One branch out of the diamond leads to $8 and the other to $14, and the branch labels match the condition. If the diamond asks 'age < 13', the yes branch must reach $8 and the no branch $14; if it asks 'age >= 13', the mapping is reversed. Deny if a price is missing, both branches carry the same price, or the prices are swapped relative to the condition.

rubric.title: Both branches lead onward to the End
rubric.description: Neither branch is a dead end — following either answer out of the diamond eventually reaches the End oval, whether the two paths rejoin at a shared 'print the price' step or each prints separately before ending. Deny only if a branch stops with nothing after it.

rubric.title: Shapes are used for what they mean
rubric.description: Ovals are used only for Start and End, the diamond is used only for the question, and rectangles (or input/output parallelograms) carry the actions. Deny if, for example, the question is drawn in a rectangle or an action is drawn in a diamond.
